clue.text: Dangerous reptile flusters hack regularly visiting north-east

parts.note: to rattle someone is to fluster them, so rattles means flusters

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so these letters go inside the compass point

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone flusters a hack journalist on a trip to north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes AK from hack, and 'visiting' puts AK between the N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattlesnakes are venomous American pit vipers whose bite can kill, so they are dangerous reptiles.

clue.text: Defiant chap entering further exam

indicators.note: to enter is to go into a place, so the chap goes inside the exam word

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken again

explanation.surface: A rebellious young man turns up to sit his exam again.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords use any short man's name for 'chap'; here it has to be one that fits inside the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone who will not give way.

clue.text: European citizen making cuts in opera?

definitions.meaning: a Spaniard, specifically a resident of a city in Andalusia
the man's trade is cutting hair
he is the title character of a Rossini comic opera

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe is trimming an opera down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making cuts in opera' reads as editing a score; the cuts are haircuts, and the opera is the title. There is no separate wordplay: the whole clue describes Figaro.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro, the title character of Rossini's opera, is a barber living in Seville.

clue.text: Turner's device Henry invested in tardily

indicators.note: to invest someone is to clothe them in robes, so Henry is wrapped in the word for tardily

parts.note: to arrive tardily is to arrive late
H = henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A painter's apparatus in which a Henry has belatedly invested.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner; here it is a woodturner.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a turner shapes wood or metal by spinning it on this machine.

clue.text: He's pressed hard, surprisingly, to find an animal minder

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A man under heavy pressure, oddly, turns out to look after animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' sets up a man, and the answer is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: she minds a flock of sheep.

clue.text: Rival church leader's hint in article? Not at all

indicators.note: in places the hint inside the word for 'Not at all'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a hint lies in an article about a rival church leader, answered with a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark fakes a question; 'Not at all' is just the slangy no, which follows the article and swallows the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical term: a rival claimant to the papacy, set up against the elected pope.

clue.text: Additional time welcomed by girl left outside union

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so the girl's name takes the time letter inside

explanation.surface: A girl is left out of a trade union but welcomed for some extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: Union reads as a trade union; it is the union of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is a union, and the Latin extra means outside, so this is a literal gloss.

clue.text: Old friend talked of spirit's shimmering effect

indicators.note: what is talked of is spoken, so the word for spirit is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: essence = spirit, the core nature of a thing

explanation.surface: An old friend describes the shimmer of a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests a ghost or a drink; it means essence, the heart of a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Named from the gem: the milky, shifting sheen of an opal.

clue.text: Walk across street, supporting deliveries on cycle, perhaps?

indicators.note: a support holds something up from below, and in a down answer the street sits under the deliveries

parts.note: in cricket a set of six deliveries (balls) from one bowler
what you have on a bicycle

explanation.surface: A pedestrian crosses a street while someone delivers on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries looks like parcels on a bike; it is cricket, where a bowler's six balls make one unit of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal compound: to stride over, so to cross on foot.

clue.text: Tree some vandal deracinated

indicators.note: some of means only part of, so the answer is a run of letters from the words that follow

parts.note: the end of vandal and the start of deracinated

explanation.surface: A vandal has pulled up a tree by its roots.
explanation.walkthrough: Deracinated means uprooted, which suits the tree but is only a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Soldier in outskirts of Epsom, overtaken and surrounded

indicators.note: the soldier goes in the outskirts letters
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters, E and M
an NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier
passed means overtaken, as on a road

explanation.surface: A soldier on the edge of Epsom is overtaken and hemmed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is a Surrey town known for its racecourse; only its edge letters are used, holding the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to surround or enclose, so encompassed means surrounded.

clue.text: Dry clinic oddly shaped like a tube

indicators.note: arranged oddly means put in a strange order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A teetotal clinic has been built in the shape of a tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' often means take the odd letters; here it simply means rearranged, and the fodder is exactly nine letters.

clue.text: Memo causing upset to college

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, and in a down answer the word is turned upside down

parts.note: Eton, the English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A memo has caused a stir at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the crossword's usual college.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short written message.

clue.text: Seamstress beheaded in jug?

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

explanation.surface: A seamstress has been beheaded in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is slang for prison, which gives the grisly surface; the question mark flags that the jug here is the pitcher kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a large wide-mouthed jug, once used with a washbasin.

clue.text: Last of kids shut up, being exhausted!

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A parent finally gets the kids to shut up and collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: Shut up reads as a demand for quiet; it means confined, as in pent-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a spent force or a spent runner.

clue.text: Limited object the French authorise

indicators.note: something limited is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an entity is a thing, an object

explanation.surface: A limited company objects to what the French authorities sanction.
explanation.walkthrough: Limited suggests a company; it only tells you to trim the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to give someone the right to do something.

clue.text: Month a boxer initially talked about a liquid measure

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer spent a month talking about how much liquid he drank.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali is the crossword's standard boxer, and 'a boxer' is one piece, not A plus a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of volume: deca- means ten, so it is ten litres.

clue.text: Interplanetary craft ultimately needs steps with it

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A spacecraft ends up needing boarding steps to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like a link meaning 'as well'; it is slang for trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a vehicle for travel between planets.

clue.text: A singular type intended to dispose of a potpourri

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a sort is a type or kind

indicators.note: to dispose of says the following a is thrown out of the word for intended

explanation.surface: Someone means to throw out a jar of potpourri of one particular kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed collection of things, so it is a synonym of a varied mixture.

clue.text: Old king's turbulent son faced sword there

definitions.note: the definition carries the surface's possessive ('s = is); the answer is the king himself

indicators.note: turbulent means in violent disorder, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An old king's rebellious son has a sword drawn against him.
explanation.walkthrough: A long anagram in a scene of royal violence; the king in question was famously pious rather than warlike.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was an Anglo-Saxon king of England from 1042 to 1066.

clue.text: Cable English member absorbed in public vehicle

indicators.note: the letters are absorbed into the vehicle, going inside it

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A cable car's English passenger loses a limb aboard a tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like wire or a cable car, but it is the old name for a message sent by telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is an old word for a telegram, a message sent by telegraph wire.

clue.text: Vicious dog accompanying a Republican judge

indicators.note: to accompany is to go along with, so the dog is placed next to the other pieces

explanation.surface: A Republican judge arrives with a savage dog at his side.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog comes first in the clue but last in the answer; accompanying only says the pieces go together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who settles a dispute.

clue.text: Fairly lofty Tudor composer overcoming height

indicators.note: to overcome is literally to come over, and in a down answer the composer sits above the height letter

parts.note: Thomas Tallis, composer to the Tudor court

explanation.surface: A Tudor composer rises above his difficulties to reach a lofty height.
explanation.walkthrough: Byrd is the other Tudor composer crosswords use; only one of them starts with a word for lofty.
explanation.definitionFit: The -ish suffix means fairly, and tall means lofty.

clue.text: Extremely popular breezy-sounding plain

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the first and last letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of PopulaR

indicators.note: sounding like means heard rather than seen, so the word for breezy is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A plain that is very popular for its fresh breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective meaning simple; it is a noun, flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical term: the vast grassy plains of North America.

clue.text: Cheap informal English comedian entertaining small number

definitions.note: informal is a dictionary label: using economic to mean cheap is colloquial

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the comedian holds the small number inside

parts.note: no. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A cheap English comic plays to a tiny audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informal' belongs with Cheap, like a dictionary label, not with the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: something economic gives good value, so it is cheap.

clue.text: A newlywed taking in garments at first to shorten

indicators.note: the newlywed takes in, or holds, the letter inside the word

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married

indicators.note: only the first letter of garments is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' looks like dressmaking, which suits the bridal surface, but it signals putting one letter inside another word.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to cut down a text, condensing it, so it means to shorten.

clue.text: Trio mostly raving originally about sick suspense story

indicators.note: the shortened trio goes about, or around, the word for sick
most of the word, losing its final letter
originally points to the first letter of raving

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trio' must be turned into the number word before 'mostly' trims it; the trimmed word then goes round the word for sick.

clue.text: Disclose how age impaired a futile mission

indicators.note: something impaired is damaged, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to reveal how getting old has weakened them, a pointless task.
explanation.walkthrough: Disclose looks like the instruction to reveal something hidden; it is only letters for the anagram.

clue.text: Hospital doctor principally employing this form of communication

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the first letters are taken

clue.text: Muslim legal expert's everyday clothing

definitions.meaning: a scholar who issues rulings on Islamic law
civilian clothes worn by someone who normally wears uniform

explanation.surface: A question of what an Islamic jurist wears day to day.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing plain clothes is British usage, chiefly of soldiers or schoolchildren out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are one word: the jurist's title, and the plain dress said to come from his image on the stage.

clue.text: Note gun covering Tyler's power unit

parts.note: me (or mi), the third note of the sol-fa scale

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A gunman keeps Tyler covered as he reaches for his power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyler's first name is wanted: Wat Tyler, leader of the English Peasants' Revolt.

clue.text: Unusually nasty adverse mark for use of language

parts.note: a cross, the mark for a wrong answer

explanation.walkthrough: The anagram stops at nasty; the cross is added on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose gloss: syntax is the way words are arranged, one aspect of how language is used.

clue.text: Hardy character's suitor carrying light by day

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the suitor holds the other pieces inside
by means next to, so the day letter sits beside the word for light

parts.note: to light on = to land on, alight

explanation.walkthrough: Light is a verb, as a bird lights on a branch; the novel is Hardy's The Woodlanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Thomas Hardy's novel The Woodlanders is about people of a Dorset wood.

clue.text: Ring and cancel film

parts.note: to annul a marriage or law is to cancel it

explanation.surface: Someone phones up and calls off a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a phone call; it is a small circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical term in architecture and heraldry, from Latin anulus, a little ring.

clue.text: Stingy governor in church, economical about energy

indicators.note: the governor goes in the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a governor

indicators.note: the economical word goes about, or around, the energy letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.walkthrough: A governor is addressed as His Excellency, and the Church of England is the usual church abbreviation.

clue.text: Silver-haired poet picked up top journalist

parts.note: Thomas Gray, of the Elegy in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A silver-haired poet is picked up by the chief journalist.

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grey hair and silver hair are the same thing.

clue.text: Broadcast by artisans dismissing first of such service personnel

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

the first of a word is its opening letter

clue.text: Reduce size of quiet skating venue

explanation.surface: A quiet ice rink is being made smaller.

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shrink something is to make it smaller.

clue.text: Urge to take Liberal inside preserved Arab area

clue.text: Book miners once found outside a hotel

explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets' books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Like some aquatic animals oddly imposing for one I ignored

explanation.definitionFit: Sponges have a porous, spongiform structure, so creatures shaped like sponges can be called spongiform.

clue.text: Scallywag taking photograph of one applying lash?

explanation.surface: A rascal takes a photo of someone wielding a whip.

clue.text: Reactive element is a must, somehow, under river

clue.text: Clear first of plants I culled ineptly

clue.text: Obstruction set back lead communications satellite

clue.text: Giant, one primarily attending a fairy queen

clue.text: Boredom initially encompassing Greek character in part of UK

clue.text: Polluted atmosphere originally stifling cat
